newsitem.title: UK: BA union says makes last call to management.
newsitem.headline: BA union says makes last call to management.

text.p: The main union involved in a dispute with British Airways Plc said on Tuesday it was making a last bid to negotiate with management before deciding later in the day whether strikes would go ahead.

"The position is we're making one last effort to get BA management to agree to talks about both the cabin crew and ground staff disputes," a spokesman for the Transport and General Workers Union (T&G) told Reuters.

He said T&G general secretary Bill Morris would telephone BA's chief executive Robert Ayling later today about resolving strike threats from cabin crew in a long-running pay dispute and from ground staff in a separate row over BA's plans to sell off its catering division.
The union said it expected to decide by around 1600 GMT at the latest about whether to give the go-ahead for industrial action on both fronts.

BA cabin crew have already agreed a series of 72-hour strikes while ground staff representatives are holding meetings to decide what action to take after members voted decisively for industrial action.
BA have said they are prepared to talk to the union about resolving issues with ground staff but were being "very tough" about the cabin crew, the T&G spokesman said.

"We're saying there's no point in having half a settlement and half a dispute, we need to get the whole thing sorted out," he said, warning that the airline risked losing the confidence of the travelling public if there was no overall solution to the dispute.
The T&G's Morris said earlier on Wednesday that BA was trying to pick off the cabin crew against the ground staff.
